keybinds: key.vanillaplusadditions.debug_overlay.toggle - en_us "Toggle Debug Overlay", de_de "Debug-Overlay umschalten"; default GLFW_KEY_KP_ADD (numpad +, InputConstants.Type.KEYSYM), category key.categories.vanillaplusadditions ("Vanilla+ Additions"); rebindable in the vanilla Controls screen (DebugOverlayKeybinds.java:18-22). It is the only VPA keybind defaulting to numpad + (repo-wide grep for GLFW_KEY_KP_ADD returns this one line), so no out-of-the-box conflict. Toggling prints the action-bar message "Debug overlay: ON/OFF" (message.vanillaplusadditions.debug_overlay.on/.off) and works without goggles and even while the module is disabled in config; the goggles check only gates what gets drawn.
oneLiner: Wear Engineer's Goggles and press numpad + to switch on the mod's shared debug view - chunk-loader borders, Chunk Anchor areas and the guardian pets' extended stat boxes all appear and disappear together with this one key.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Supplies the Engineer's Goggles recognised by GogglesItem.isWearingGoggles(player), which also accepts goggles worn in a Curios slot (Create registers that predicate itself). Without Create the only remaining path is an item from the vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles tag in the vanilla HEAD slot (Curios is not consulted there) - and since the tag's create:goggles entry is required:false, it silently drops out without Create, leaving only Create: Aeronautics' aviator's goggles. The module still loads and the keybind still works; the GogglesItem call sits behind the static CREATE_LOADED = ModList.get().isLoaded("create") flag, so it is never resolved when Create is absent. Declared type="optional" in the bundle's mods.toml; the module does NOT override shouldInitialize().

shortDescription: Shared goggles debug overlay framework (toggle + chunk borders, cat stats, ...).
notes:
SCOPE / WHAT IT IS
- Pure client-side framework module: no items, blocks, entities, commands, recipes, loot tables, network payloads and no mixins. Verified by grep over modules/debug_overlay/ for DeferredRegister / RegisterCommandsEvent / CustomPacketPayload / EntityType / BlockEntityType (zero hits), by the absence of any debug_overlay entry in src/main/resources/vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json, and by build.gradle:420, where the standalone descriptor carries neither dataGlobs nor mixins.
- Everything lives in modules/debug_overlay/client/ behind @EventBusSubscriber(value = Dist.CLIENT). DebugOverlayModule.onInitialize() (DebugOverlayModule.java:27-31) has an empty body with two comment lines.
- Config: constructed with AbstractModuleConfig::createDefault (DebugOverlayModule.java:24) -> DefaultModuleConfig, whose body is nothing but the comment "// Keine zusaetzliche Konfiguration erforderlich" (AbstractModuleConfig.java:198-208). Hence zero module-specific keys; only the universal `enabled` + `debug_logging` that AbstractModuleConfig.buildConfig() adds for every module (AbstractModuleConfig.java:57-66).
- enabledByDefault = true comes from the interface default Module.isEnabledByDefault() (Module.java:73-75); DebugOverlayModule does not override it (the repo's only override is HauntedHouseModule.java:116).

BIGGEST GOTCHA: the module's own `enabled` switch does NOT turn this framework off.
Both handler classes register via @EventBusSubscriber annotations (DebugOverlayKeybinds.java:15, DebugOverlayClientEvents.java:20), which NeoForge scans per jar regardless of VPA's ModuleManager, and nothing anywhere in modules/debug_overlay/ calls isModuleEnabled(). With debug_overlay.enabled = false the keybind is still registered, Numpad + still flips the state and still prints the ON/OFF action-bar message, and every already-registered renderer still draws. What IS gated is the consumer side: ModuleManager.clientSetup() iterates only enabledModules (ModuleManager.java:161-175), so a disabled minecart_chunk_loading / stationary_chunk_loader / train_chunk_loading never registers its renderer. A doc writer must not promise that disabling debug_overlay removes the keybind.

ACTIVATION GATE (DebugOverlayClientEvents.active(), lines 85-91) - all three must hold:
1. DebugOverlayState.isEnabled() (the Numpad + toggle),
2. mc.player != null && mc.level != null,
3. GogglesUtil.isWearingGoggles(mc.player).
Registered renderers therefore never re-check toggle or goggles (documented in DebugOverlayRenderer's javadoc, lines 10-16). IMPORTANT ORDERING DETAIL: the keybind is consumed BEFORE that gate - the consumeClick loop sits at DebugOverlayClientEvents.java:29-36, the active() check only at line 38 - so Numpad + toggles the state and prints the action-bar message even without goggles. docs/modules/cat_guardian.md:165-166 already states exactly this ("The keybind can be toggled even without goggles equipped"). The toggle is a plain static boolean, never persisted and never synced, so it is OFF again after every client restart (DebugOverlayState.java:9 plus class javadoc).

WHO ACTUALLY PLUGS IN (registry vs. shared toggle) - this is narrower than the shortDescription implies:
- Via DebugOverlayRegistry.register() inside their onClientSetup(): minecart_chunk_loading (MinecartChunkLoadingModule.java:106-112), stationary_chunk_loader (StationaryChunkLoaderModule.java:101-108), train_chunk_loading (TrainChunkLoadingModule.java:117-123). That is the complete list.
- NOT via the registry: cat_guardian, axolotl_guardian and mob_cart_loader run their own client handlers and merely READ DebugOverlayState.isEnabled() / GogglesUtil.isWearingGoggles() (CatGuardianGogglesClientHandler.java:100,216; AxolotlGuardianGogglesClientHandler.java:104,214; MobCartGogglesClientHandler.java:41). So "cat stats" share the keybind but are not registered DebugOverlayRenderers. Note that mob_cart_loader is registered in the bundle (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:184) but has NO standalone descriptor in build.gradle at all, so its goggles panel exists only in the bundle jar.

RENDER PIPELINE DETAILS worth documenting
- World rendering runs at RenderLevelStageEvent.Stage.AFTER_TRANSLUCENT_BLOCKS (DebugOverlayClientEvents.java:48-50); the framework pushes a PoseStack already translated by -cameraPos (line 61-62), so renderers use raw world coordinates, and it flushes DEPTH_LINES, DEPTH_QUADS, XRAY_LINES, XRAY_QUADS afterwards (lines 68-71). The level-stage handler additionally returns early when the registry is empty (line 52); clientTick and renderHud just iterate an empty list.
- DebugRenderUtil exposes four RenderTypes: XRAY_LINES (line 22) / XRAY_QUADS (line 40) with NO_DEPTH_TEST, and DEPTH_LINES (line 57) / DEPTH_QUADS (line 74) with LEQUAL_DEPTH_TEST, plus helpers renderChunkBorder (two overloads, lines 96 and 108; the 4-flag one lets callers suppress shared internal walls so fills don't stack into fog) and renderBox (line 142).
- Because all three registered renderers use the DEPTH_ types, what the framework itself draws is occluded by terrain - it is NOT an x-ray view. Only the non-registry handlers (cat_guardian, axolotl_guardian) draw see-through, and they do it with their own private RenderTypes.

DEAD / STALE CODE (all provable)
- DebugOverlayState.setEnabled(boolean) (line 23) is never called anywhere in src/main/java - dead API surface.
- DebugRenderUtil.XRAY_LINES and XRAY_QUADS are never written to by any renderer in the repo; they are only endBatch()-flushed (DebugOverlayClientEvents.java:70-71). All in-repo consumers use the DEPTH_ variants (ChunkLoaderBorderRenderer.java:80-81, AnchorBorderRenderer.java:58-59, ChunkLoaderTrackBorderRenderer.java:91-92), while arm_target_overlay (:44), block_glow (:48), cat_guardian (:40) and axolotl_guardian (:48) each define their OWN private XRAY_LINES RenderType instead of reusing the shared one - a de-duplication opportunity, and a reason not to describe the shared xray types as "used by the cat overlay".
- DebugRenderUtil's class javadoc (lines 15-18) still claims "Both render types are depth-test-free ('xray')" - stale since the DEPTH_ variants were added; the file now has four types, two of them depth-tested.
- DebugOverlayRegistry.renderers() (line 22-24) returns the mutable internal ArrayList (no unmodifiable wrapper / defensive copy); register() (line 16-20) de-dupes via List.contains, i.e. by equals/identity, so two distinct instances of the same renderer class would both be added.
- No TODO/FIXME/HACK comments in the module.

GOGGLES GATE / OPTIONAL-MOD DETAIL
GogglesUtil.isWearingGoggles() (lines 29-37) first tries Create's GogglesItem.isWearingGoggles(player) behind the static CREATE_LOADED = ModList.get().isLoaded("create") flag (line 25) - that path also honours goggles in a Curios slot, because Create itself registers that predicate - and otherwise falls back to "item in EquipmentSlot.HEAD is in the vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles tag" (line 36). The Curios path applies only to Create's own goggles; the tag check is hard-wired to the vanilla HEAD slot. Both tag entries are "required": false (arm_goggles.json:3 create:goggles, :4 aeronautics:aviators_goggles), so on an install without Create AND without Create: Aeronautics the tag resolves to an EMPTY set and the overlay can never become active - that holds even in the all-in-one bundle, not just in standalone jars.

STANDALONE-JAR TRAP
build.gradle:420 lists debug_overlay with no dataGlobs, while the arm_goggles tag JSON is assigned to the arm_target_overlay jar (build.gradle:387-388), and coreJar ships only assets/vanillaplusadditions/** , not data/** (build.gradle:617). So in a standalone install that has vpa_debug_overlay but neither Create nor vpa_arm_target_overlay, the vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles tag has no content at all -> the fallback check can never match. In the bundle the tag file is present (src/main/resources/data/vanillaplusadditions/tags/item/arm_goggles.json), subject to the required:false caveat above. The generated standalone mods.toml (renderModuleToml, build.gradle:507-535) declares only vpa_core / neoforge / minecraft as required plus an "incompatible" entry against the bundle modId vanillaplusadditions; it declares NO create dependency at all, not even optional. Entrypoint: standalone/debug_overlay/DebugOverlayStandalone.java, @Mod("vpa_debug_overlay") -> StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot(), which registers the single-module COMMON config spec (StandaloneModuleBootstrap.java:40-46).

README CONTRADICTIONS (README.md as of this commit)
- Line 230's compatibility-table row for debug_overlay is correct.
- Lines 243-247 are outdated, and the previous fact sheet got the corrected number wrong too: FIVE standalone module jars declare moduleDeps ['vpa_debug_overlay'] - axolotl_guardian (build.gradle:393), cat_guardian (:403, together with vpa_flying_fish), minecart_chunk_loading (:446), stationary_chunk_loader (:456) and train_chunk_loading (:461). The README names only three (vpa_cat_guardian plus "the two chunk loaders").
- The prose at README.md:163-164 is a fair summary, but see the registry-vs-toggle distinction above.

DOCS STATUS
- There is no docs/modules/debug_overlay.md (and no docs/debug_overlay.md) - this module has never had its own doc page, and the README's Documentation section links none. The keybind IS documented, however, inside another module's page: docs/modules/cat_guardian.md:159-166 (default NumPad +, rebindable, works without goggles). Further prose: README.md:163-164, CHANGELOG.md:1014 (beta.16 introduction), :1009, :974 (the "libs really optional" fix that introduced the isLoaded("create") gate), :721 and :1079 (the cat-only predecessor keybind this one replaced).

There is no lang key for the module display name itself - "Debug Overlay" is the hard-coded Java string in DebugOverlayModule.java:22.
